risks.title: The comparison is only as available as the structural alignment
risks.detail: qaOnlyStyleComparison is "compared" only when alignLiveOriginal succeeded, i.e. the live site's DOM still matches the SiteSpec exactly in count, tag sequence and parent relation. On a real, actively-changing site (the linear.app / stripe pilots) many pages drift structurally, so the honest answer for them will be "unavailable (source-not-aligned)" and the QA-only tail stays unverified there. That is the correct answer rather than a fabricated 0, but it means this channel's REACH on a live production site is bounded by drift and is not yet measured on one. The suite proves the mechanism, not its yield.

risks.title: Population mismatch inside LiveFidelity
risks.detail: The neighbouring liveFidelity fields are computed over drift-FREE pages only; the QA-only counters are computed over every page that recorded a verdict (the structurally-aligned bar, which is what the pairing needs). Both the schema comment and the CLI line disclose the denominators, but a reader who assumes one population for the whole section could misread the total. An alternative was to restrict it to the drift-free subset, which would report nothing at all on most real sites.

risks.title: Document-root wrappers are never compared
risks.detail: Task 14 renders <html>/<body> as div wrappers, so compareCapturedStyles' tag guard excludes them and their QA-only properties (a body-level text-shadow or background-clip, say) are silently uncompared. The count is surfaced as qaOnlyStyleTagMismatchedNodes rather than hidden, but it is a real hole in coverage that mirrors the documentRootAdapted handling in style-diff.ts and was NOT extended here.

risks.title: The sample list is capped, the totals are not
risks.detail: qaOnlyStyleSamples is capped at 50/page and is deterministic (document order x sorted property), which means on a page with a body-inherited difference the 50 samples can all land on one property and one subtree. The uncapped qaOnlyStyleByProperty is the field to read for scope. There is no inherited-cause grouping here of the kind style-diff.ts does for the spec axis — a wrong inherited text-decoration-color would be reported once per descendant.

risks.title: Change B widens the interaction capture to 144 properties
risks.detail: TARGET_STATE_STYLE_PROPERTIES is now a strict superset of what it was, so open-state comparison can newly report differences on properties it previously ignored — including benign engine defaults. On this repo's fixture suite it changed no verdict (134/134), but the first real interaction-heavy run may surface new target-state style mismatches, and some of them will be noise rather than defects. The cost side is negligible (30 extra getPropertyValue calls on ONE element per replay side).

risks.title: Capture-time cost on the page axis is still unmeasured on a real site
risks.detail: Carried forward unchanged from the build handoff: the 30 extra properties per element per capture were never timed on a real full-site run, and this change adds a per-page O(comparable nodes x 30) string comparison on top. Both are cheap in principle; neither has a number.
